differences.what: The message discloses that the headline additive/combined number (0.265/0.2647) is computed against a self-made, cruder reproduction of the white-bear stance direction (0.2255 vs the source's own 0.83), and that the real combination with the source's actual vector may differ and that 'half the credit' for the bigger number belongs to the source (WBS/white-bear work); the write-up states the 0.265 additive result with the source's name but omits that its own anchor vector is a weaker stand-in for the source's direction and omits the credit-sharing caveat entirely.

rationale: Both documents frame content-due steering as an independent method derived from the repo's own centring theory, and both treat the white-bear/Raman stance direction only as a comparison point used to test orthogonality and additivity (cos ≈ −0.1, combined ≈0.265), not as something the method builds on or reproduces — so both sit at the 'names' level. The message adds a caveat absent from the write-up: that its own WBS/white-bear anchor vector is a cruder, self-made approximation (0.2255) of the source's actual direction (0.83), meaning the reported combined/additive headline number partly depends on this weaker proxy and that 'half the credit' for that bigger number belongs to the source, a credit/overlap nuance the write-up does not surface.
